title: Beyond-Birthday Security for Shorter-Key Six-Round KAF
summary: Key collisions cap multi-user security with one n-bit key at half the key length; proving six-round KAF beyond-birthday security with fewer than twice n bits of main key and weaker round-key independence remains open.

formal_statement.body: For six-round Key-Alternating Feistel (KAF) ciphers, prove beyond-birthday security when the main key contains fewer than $2n$ bits, ideally when a single $n$-bit main key is used, while relaxing the assumption that the round keys are independent. The problem is constrained by the fact that using only one $n$-bit main key gives at most $n/2$-bit multi-user security because an attacker can exploit key collisions, so a successful result must account for this limitation.

scope.domain: Security of six-round Key-Alternating Feistel block ciphers with reduced main-key material and less independent round keys.
assumptions: Round-key independence is the assumption targeted for relaxation.
parameters: n: size parameter governing the main-key lengths and the stated multi-user security ceiling
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish beyond-birthday security with fewer than 2n main-key bits, ideally a single n-bit key, after relaxing round-key independence while accounting for the n/2-bit multi-user ceiling caused by key collisions.

citations.label: Revisiting Key-Alternating Feistel Ciphers for Shorter Keys and Multi-user Security

progress.summary: The source presents this as a concrete direction for improving its six-round result by reducing the main-key length and dropping round-key independence. It identifies key-collision attacks as limiting multi-user security with a single n-bit key to half the key length.
citation_labels: Chun Guo et al., Revisiting Key-Alternating Feistel Ciphers for Shorter Keys and Multi-user Security
